P1.evidence: Setter notes referenced rather than read back — 'I've already heard a good amount of things from Kim. But I would love to hear everything from you' — though he did use a specific detail from Kim later ('I heard from Kim that you've been doing kettlebells for like a week now'). Frame was two-part: 'go over where you are, where you want to go. See if we can fit in there perfectly. If we can, will take you through how, okay?' — no what's-in-the-way, no what-you-need. Agreement asked and given. Open question ran: 'tell me, what can we potentially help you out with, Dale?'

P2.evidence: The most thorough baseline in the batch. Pain was interrogated properly — location, trigger pattern, and a 1-10 severity scale ('on a scale from 1 to 10... whereabouts do you think that it's at?' — 4 or 5) — followed by 'Have you gotten injured before?', which produced the sciatica, the prior shoulder injury and the runner's knee. Age asked directly. Training week established and corrected ('You go to the gym six times a week, right? What is it?'). Results from the current week asked ('do you feel like this is actually helping?'). Full diet run-through with the snacking probe that surfaced a nightly pint of ice cream. Energy asked explicitly. Gaps: height and weight never asked despite fat loss being a goal; occupation never asked, only his commute times for scheduling; no health-conditions or hereditary question; and no sleep question, which matters given nightly sugar before bed — the rep even asserted the effect on sleep without ever asking about it.

P3.evidence: Ran deep. The bridge was asked properly: 'why do you feel like it's now the time for you to actually double down on fixing it? Because there's so many people who are 36, 37, and they're like, oh, it comes with age.' The future-state question ran twice, once at six months to a year and again projected to 46, and it drove through to legacy — 'I'd be able to teach them the stuff that I learned' — 'Passing it on.' The reflect-back landed and was confirmed: 'do you agree with those thoughts?' — 'Yes, I do.' Missing: a specific physical thing he cannot do right now, and an explicit who-else-does-this-impact question — the children came up because he raised them.

P4.evidence: Asked whether he had ever had a trainer ('no, never had') and got the consequence in his own words: 'I've always done things on my own... And I feel like I'm paying the price now with my body.' The root cause was properly excavated — the compulsion to train daily, the overtraining, the injuries — and the prospect named the gap himself when asked what he would need: 'holding me accountable to doing less and doing it the right way.' The rep then reframed it accurately: 'now we just got to hold you back a little bit.' Only the scripted information-isn't-the-problem line is absent, and this prospect's gap genuinely was structure rather than information.

P5.evidence: The strongest consequence frame in the batch. 'Let's say don't do anything with it, and it keeps on going in the same way it's currently going... where do you feel like you would be at in five years from now?' produced a vivid answer — a doctor, surgery, 'stuck in this cycle of trying to fix things on my own and really not getting anywhere.' Then the look-back ('what would you then think at that point?' — 'I'd probably regret not making the changes') and the settle question ('do you feel like you're willing to settle for looking back in five years?' — 'No. No.'). Only the line-in-the-sand ask is missing.

P6.evidence: Both questions ran after the pillars: 'if we get all of that in place, that there would be anything besides that would stop you?' — 'No' — and 'do you feel like, yes, this was exactly what I'm looking for, and I want to do this?' The answer was hedged with nervousness, and the rep correctly did not steamroll it; he worked it with the military analogy until the prospect agreed the nervousness was normal, then confirmed. A clear yes was in hand before price was named. The one structural criticism belongs to the process, not the phase: the commitment was secured before anyone had established that the prospect could pay, which is why a full close attempt collapsed at 00:31:46.

P11.evidence: A payment link was sent and confirmed received ('Yeah, I just got the link'), which is further than most calls in this batch reach, but no payment was collected and the prospect retracted the agreement minutes later. The onboarding call was attempted and failed on logistics — the only slots offered were 7:15am and 10:45am Hawaii time, both inside his working hours, and the rep ended up saying 'I will ask him for different times' with nothing booked. No agreement email, nothing signed, no welcome email, no Skool link, no questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete run of this play in the batch. Isolate ran ('outside of the investment, do you feel like, yes, is this something I want to do... is it just the investment that's stopping you?') and was repeated later in the should-versus-how form ('is it more of like, it's just quite a bit, we need to figure out how to actually make it work? Or is it more of like, I just don't want to invest in it myself?'). Financial picture: monthly surplus after expenses ($400-500), cash set aside (about $6,000 in savings), credit score (740-750). Not run: the permission ask before opening the financial conversation, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto or investments. He also handled the savings disclosure carefully — 'I'm not saying that we should use it' — but then proposed financing against credit instead, which is the substantive problem with how this play closed out.

Trigger at 00:25:46, 'I'm excited, but I'm also nervous at the same time, because it's something I've never done.' The rep ran the play well and in the prospect's own language: asked him to name a previous nervous first, got the military, and used it — 'when you went in there, were you like 100% sure this is the right thing? No. And well, you're still alive, right?' — then reframed the nervousness as evidence the thing matters: 'if you wouldn't be feeling anything, I would tell you this is probably not the right thing for you to do.' The objection resolved and did not return.

Trigger at 00:34:31, 'this is something I kind of need to think about.' Ran: the can-this-get-you-there test in its worth form, asked twice and correctly separated from timing — 'do you feel like that outcome is worth six grand to you if you do it now or in a year?' Not run: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', the different-decision question, the man-you-want-to-be question, and the final are-you-sure. He moved to a cheaper product rather than finishing the play.

Two script gaps, both live on this call. First, the clinical one the playbook already knows about: a prospect with worsening multi-site pain, sciatica and hand numbness and no clinician involved has no scripted path, and the rep improvised entirely toward the sale. Second, the cheaper-substitute gap: this prospect was already getting results from Trevor's free YouTube videos after one week — 'I already feel better. I'm not as stiff' — and there is no play for a free version of your own product that is visibly working.

notes: Process-wise this is the strongest call in the batch — baseline, goals, root cause, consequence and commitment all genuinely ran, and the fear play was handled well. Two things undo it. Affordability was never touched until after a full close attempt, so forty minutes of work collapsed on a number that one early question would have surfaced. And when it did collapse, the answer was consumer credit at roughly the prospect's entire monthly surplus, followed by a price that does not exist yet.
